name: TESSERA Corponation Sentinel Compact SDC-1 'Aegis'
description:
The Sentinel Compact SDC-1 is TESSERA Corponation's flagship personal defense instrument for the executive and high-net-worth individual market — a precision-engineered multi-mode aerosol device that integrates three distinct operational compounds into a single palm-sized unit with electronic mode selection. The SDC-1's three modes are accessible via a capacitive selector ring: Mode 1 deploys a TESSERA-proprietary OC concentrate (TS-Capsaicinoid-7, rated at 4.2 million SHU equivalent) for direct physical deterrence; Mode 2 activates a UV-fluorescent and DNA-binding marking compound with a seventy-two-hour skin persistence that survives standard washing and links to TESSERA's Sentinel ID database for law enforcement recovery; Mode 3 emits a precisely tuned electromagnetic pulse aerosol designed to disrupt unshielded consumer-grade BCI devices, producing immediate sensory disconnection, disorientation, and temporary interface blindness in BCI-dependent subjects.

The device's housing is machined from aerospace-grade titanium with a brushed finish and is available in four colorways. It is biometrically locked to the registered owner's fingerprint and BCI signature — an unauthorized user receives a 40,000-volt contact deterrent from the grip surface. The SDC-1 is sold exclusively through TESSERA Authorized Dispensaries and requires registration to the purchaser's TESSERA account, which bundles a Sentinel Monitoring subscription that logs all deployment events and provides automatic law enforcement notification on Mode 1 or 3 activation.

The BCI disruption mode has generated significant controversy. TESSERA maintains that Mode 3 is calibrated to affect only unshielded consumer-grade interfaces, but independent security researchers have documented cases where it produced lasting interface damage in subjects with older or modified BCI hardware. TESSERA's legal team has successfully characterized all documented injuries as resulting from 'non-standard BCI configurations outside the product's design parameters.'
legality: Licensed — registered civilian ownership permitted for Tier 4+ verified individuals; BCI disruption mode (Mode 3) restricted in public spaces under Meridian Electromagnetic Interference Ordinance, though enforcement is inconsistent
specifications:
Mode 1 (OC): TS-Capsaicinoid-7 at 4.2M SHU equivalent, stream 3.5m effective
Mode 2 (Marking): UV-fluorescent DNA-binding compound, 72-hour skin persistence
Mode 3 (BCI Disruption): tuned EM aerosol, effective 1.5m radius
Mode selection: capacitive ring, 0.3-second switch time
Security: biometric lock (fingerprint + BCI signature); unauthorized contact: 40kV deterrent
Canister capacity: 6 bursts per mode (shared reservoir, software-apportioned)
Housing: aerospace titanium, 4 colorways
Weight: 0.09 kg
Dimensions: 9cm × 2.8cm
Connectivity: TESSERA Sentinel Monitoring subscription (mandatory)
Price: Φ3,800
tactical_use: The SDC-1 is designed for the specific threat profile of a Tier 4 executive or high-net-worth individual: a close-quarters confrontation with a potentially augmented assailant where the user cannot or will not carry a conventional firearm. The recommended deployment sequence is Mode 3 first to disrupt BCI-dependent situational awareness and chrome coordination, followed immediately by Mode 1 OC to the face, with Mode 2 activated on any physical contact to ensure prosecution evidence. TESSERA's Sentinel training program sells a companion course that teaches this sequence as a three-step 'executive response protocol.'
cultural_context: The SDC-1 is a status object as much as a weapon — being seen to carry one signals both wealth and a certain paranoid preparedness that is fashionable in Tier 4 corporate circles. 'Running the Triple' refers to using all three modes in sequence. In lower tiers, the Aegis is resented as the embodiment of a system where the wealthy can legally carry what amounts to a BCI attack device while Shelf residents are arrested for possessing basic OC spray. Underground BCI hardware vendors have begun marketing 'Aegis-hardened' shielding packages in direct response.
known_users: Tier 4 and Tier 5 executives and high-net-worth individuals
story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive was found dead — Mode 2 marking compound on both hands suggests they deployed their Aegis before dying, but TESSERA's Sentinel database shows no deployment event was logged

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, pen-sized aerosol device with the refined minimalism of luxury corpo tech. The form factor suggests precision engineering over tactical bulk—this is a tool for boardrooms and penthouse suites, not field operatives. The capacitive selector ring dominates the midline, glowing subtly when powered. Compact enough to palm entirely, yet commanding visual presence through its material authority.
physical_description.dimensions: 90mm length × 28mm diameter (cylindrical body); selector ring adds 3mm radial depth
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively dense for its size. The aerospace titanium imparts satisfying heft—0.09 kg feels substantial in the hand, suggesting engineered gravitas rather than true heaviness. Perfectly balanced for single-handed precision control.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade titanium alloy; internal pressure vessel; precision-machined nozzle assembly
physical_description.finish: Brushed titanium with a satin sheen that resists fingerprints and reflections. The surface has a controlled, almost clinical smoothness—no aggressive texturing or tactical knurling. This is executive restraint weaponized.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte titanium silver-grey. Accent: the capacitive selector ring in one of four colorways (Charcoal, Obsidian, Moonstone, or Champagne chrome). The nozzle tip shows barely visible secondary charging ports in contrasting anodized finish.
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth, contoured titanium body with ergonomic finger indexing—no aggressive grip texture, but tactile enough to prevent slip. The biometric activation zone feels warmer than the surrounding metal, hinting at embedded contact sensors. Deliberately civilian, never tactical.
distinctive_features: Capacitive selector ring with soft LED indicators (one indicator per mode, glows briefly on activation)
Biometric lock plate along the lower grip—almost invisible, just a subtle panel break in the titanium
Dual secondary vents near the nozzle assembly (for Mode 3 aerosol dispersal)
Micro-stamped TESSERA branding and regulatory compliance marks on the lower barrel
Faint thermal indicator strip that shows canister pressure (embedded in rear third)
Charging port (USB-C) recessed into the bottom cap with magnetic alignment
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA CORPONATION logo (geometric shield) laser-etched into the upper barrel, right side. Serial number and regulatory stamps (Meridian Compliance, GLMZ Tier 4+) on the lower rear. Microscopic QR code on the activation cap linking to the Sentinel Monitoring subscription database.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine, rarely field-used. Most SDC-1s are maintained in executive condition—polished, registered, and active on Sentinel Monitoring subscriptions. If deployed, shows minimal wear; if used extensively (rare), the titanium develops micro-scratches and the LED indicators may show uneven degradation.
